safescout.name: SafeScout
safescout.title: Risk-Limiting Active Perception for Autonomous UAV Landslide Assessment Under Distribution Shift
safescout.question: How can an autonomous UAV use calibrated uncertainty and hazard consequence to decide where to inspect next, reducing critical misses under a limited flight-time budget?
problem: Disaster monitoring needs more than detecting objects or hazards.
An autonomous drone has to recognise when its predictions are uncertain, judge whether an uncertain area might be dangerous, and decide whether looking again is worth the time and energy it has left.
safescout.honesty: SafeScout began in September 2026. There are no results, flight deployments or SafeScout publications yet. What follows is the research question and the planned approach.

loop.title: Estimate uncertainty
loop.body: Calibrated confidence, including under distribution shift.

loop.title: Weigh consequence
loop.body: How costly would a miss be here?

loop.title: Choose next view
loop.body: Spend limited flight time where it reduces risk most.

roadmap.body: Define the problem, the hazards that matter and how to measure critical misses.
Compare pretrained and fine-tuned CNN, transformer and hybrid detectors.
Test across geographically distinct datasets and calibrate confidence.
Build an inspection policy that weighs uncertainty against consequence.
Compare against random, coverage-based and uncertainty-only baselines under fixed flight budgets.

metrics: Mission efficiency under an inspection budget
safescout.supervisors: Professor Ibrahim Habli and Dr Colin Paterson
safescout.programme: UKRI Centre for Doctoral Training in Safe AI (SAINTS), University of York

publications.title: Deep Learning for Underwater Object Detection: A Comprehensive Survey of Models, Datasets, and Challenges
publications.summary: A survey of deep learning for underwater object detection covering CNN, transformer and hybrid approaches, the datasets the field relies on, how methods are benchmarked and evaluated, reproducibility, and the practical constraints of deployment.

publications.title: Deep Learning for Underwater Object Detection: From CNNs to Transformer-Based Real-Time Solutions
publications.venue: 30th International Conference on Automation and Computing (ICAC 2025)
publications.summary: Traces underwater object detection from traditional and sonar-based techniques to CNN and transformer models, with a focus on poor visibility, scarce data and real-time constraints. Contributes a six-class taxonomy and a cross-dataset speed and accuracy comparison.
